newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-ANGRY VENABLES SEEKS FIFA HELP OVER VIDUKA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANGRY VENABLES SEEKS FIFA HELP OVER VIDUKA.

text.p: Australia coach Terry Venables said on Friday he would enlist FIFA's help to force Croatia Zagreb to release striker Mark Viduka for World Cup duty next week after claiming the club had blocked his return home.
Venables said the Croatian league and cup double-winners failed to respond to several requests to make Viduka available for this month's Oceania qualifying tournament in Sydney.
The former England coach described the circumstances surrounding Viduka's absence as "a kick in the teeth" to Australia's bid to reach next year's finals in France.

"We've now gone through the FIFA route and made our presence felt in that direction quite heavily. We're looking to them for help," Venables told reporters at a news conference to announce a 26-man squad.
"It seems Mark has had a lot of pressure on him not to come. It has come from the president of his club, and maybe even higher circles than that," said Venables, who did not elaborate.

"I find it outrageous. Imagine if a club refused to let Alan Shearer play for England," said Venables, who has guided Australia to five successive wins in friendlies since taking charge late last year.
Viduka was expected to lead the attack in the first round of qualifiers against Solomon Islands and Tahiti, starting on June 11.

Venables will rely on a core of overseas-based players, including Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich, Southampton's Robbie Slater, Ned Zelic of Auxerre, West Ham midfielder Stan Lazaridis and Glasgow Rangers defender Craig Moore.
Lazio sweeper and midfielder Paul Okon was unavailable because of a knee injury.
New Zealand are expected to win the other Oceania qualifying pool.
The two Oceania group winners will face each other in a playoff, with the winner of that tie to face an Asian country in a final World Cup qualifying playoff later this year.
Goalkeepers - Mark Bosnich, Zeljko Kalac, Jason Petkovic.
Defenders - Matthew Bingley, Alex Tobin, Tony Vidmar, Milan Ivanovic, Steve Horvat, Tony Popovic, Craig Moore, Robbie Hooker, Kris Trajanovski, Kevin Muscat.
Midfielders - Robbie Slater, Stan Lazaridis, Craig Foster, Ned Zelic, Robbie Enes, Josip Skoko, Aurelio Vidmar.
Forwards - Damian Mori, Paul Trimboli, John Aloisi, Graham Arnold, Ernie Tapai, David Zdrilic.
